scope: Strict Linux backend build and cold, finite retain/readback checks on WSL2 Vulkan Dozen and physical Radeon 780M. The renderer observer uses real loaded device modules. Full original render scenes and exact-main release remain open.
replay: Extract verification.tar.gz into out/dozen-endpoint-compact. Scripts and observed logs use this scratch root.

Build study modules and link profile.cpp and profile-split.cpp against the backend archives from the baseline revision. compile-endpoint.py and compile-split.py regenerate the screens in that order. compile-endpoint.py checks the original packed stock SHA; dependency pins and the Linux qualification builds are in build.py.

Link profile-integrated.cpp against the strict backend archives from the source revision. Compile with /usr/bin/g++-14 -std=c++2c -O3 -DNDEBUG -DSIRIUS_CONTRACT_MODE=2 -DSIRIUS_HAS_RETAINED_COMPUTE=1 -DSIRIUS_RELEASE_RESOURCE_LOCKED=1 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -Wno-missing-field-initializers -Isrc -Itests. Link in order libsirius_backend_cpu.a, libsirius_backend.a, libsirius_core.a, libsirius_base.a, -lvulkan -ldl -lrt -pthread.

The individual logs give each invocation and module arguments. Use the named ICD and cold cache settings. Then run python3 out/dozen-endpoint-compact/compare-readbacks.py --integrated. The comparison binds all active output, including scratch and refused rows, and uses the existing independent 105-digit reference and its tolerances.
